title: LSP: Liskov Substitution
points: A subclass must be usable anywhere its parent is used without breaking behaviour.
A subclass should only inherit what it can actually do. If it throws or no-ops a parent method, the hierarchy is wrong.
trade: A subclass shouldn't strengthen preconditions, weaken postconditions, or throw unexpected exceptions. Classic case: Square extends Rectangle.
test: How do you spot an LSP violation in code?
answer: instanceof checks on subtypes, overrides that throw UnsupportedOperationException, or empty overrides that do nothing.

questions.question: Penguin extends Bird and overrides fly() to throw UnsupportedOperationException. Which principle is broken and what is the fix?
options: SRP: split Bird into two classes
LSP: model flying as a separate capability, so Penguin doesn't inherit fly()
DIP: inject a Flyer into Bird
questions.explanation: A subclass must work wherever its parent does. Move fly() to FlyingBird so Penguin only inherits what it can do.
